newsitem.title: USA: Couple jailed in anti-drug journalist murder case.
newsitem.headline: Couple jailed in anti-drug journalist murder case.

text.p: A Colombian couple who took part in the killing of a U.S. journalist who crusaded against drug traffickers were sentenced on Wednesday to long prison terms, although they cooperated in the murder investigation.

Juan Carlos Velasco, 28, was sentenced in Brooklyn Federal Court to 15 years' imprisonment for helping to arrange the murder of Manuel de Dios Unanue, whose writings had angered Colombia's Cali cartel.
Velasco helped hire the trigger-man who shot de Dios twice in the head four years ago in New York.
U. S. District Judge Edward Korman sentenced Velasco's wife, Elizabeth Castano, also 28, to 18 years in federal prison for helping to finger de Dios for the gunman.
The couple pleaded guilty in 1992 and had cooperated with investigators. Velasco could have received a life sentence, prosecutors said, and his wife up to 30 years.
Vicky Sanchez, who lived and worked with de Dios and is the mother of his 7-year-old daughter, had asked the judge not to take the couple's cooperation into consideration in sentencing them.

The Cuban-born de Dios, 49, was gunned down in 1992 in a restaurant in the city's borough of Queens. He was a former editor in chief of El Diario-La Prensa, New York's leading Spanish-language newspaper.
De Dios was well known for his investigations into the cocaine trade, and his murder immediately led to speculation he had been rubbed out by drug kingpins.
Of the seven people indicted for de Dios' murder, five, including Velasco and his wife, pleaded guilty. All except Velasco received 18-year sentences.

A sixth person, Wilson Mejia Velez, the gunman, was sentenced to life in prison in 1994 for the execution-style killing. A seventh, Guillermo Leon Restrepo Gaviria, who prosecutors said was paid $50,000 for the contracted assassination, is a fugitive.
